subject.title: [Bug]: openclaw agent --deliver silently drops messages (exit 0, no delivery)

question: Should `openclaw agent --deliver` remain agent-reply delivery with `openclaw message send` as the literal notification path, or should maintainers sponsor an explicit direct-delivery/session-injection surface?
rationale: Current docs and source preserve reply-delivery semantics, prior PR discussion rejected a broad semantic change, and the requested session injection crosses a security boundary that automation cannot choose safely.

options.title: Keep command boundaries split
options.body: Keep `agent --deliver` for agent-composed replies, improve suppressed-delivery status/docs as needed, and handle direct session injection in a separate security-reviewed API.

options.title: Sponsor explicit direct mode
options.body: Accept a new direct-delivery signal or command/API with compatibility notes, regression tests, and security review for session injection.

options.title: Close as not planned
options.body: Close this issue and the linked fork PR if maintainers decide `message send` is sufficient and no remaining status or session-injection work should be tracked here.

recommendation.title: Keep command boundaries split
recommendation.body: Keep `agent --deliver` for agent-composed replies, improve suppressed-delivery status/docs as needed, and handle direct session injection in a separate security-reviewed API.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete already made the clearest maintainer-facing command-boundary call on the linked same-repo PR and has recent delivery/docs history.
